issues.body: `_CARGO_INSTALL_RE = r"\bcargo\s+install\s+wasm-pack\b"` only detects commands where `wasm-pack` immediately follows `install`. Cargo accepts options before the crate argument, for example `cargo install --locked wasm-pack` or `cargo install --version 0.14.0 wasm-pack`. Such a workflow command is a real install site but contributes neither a site nor an offence; because the repository has other recognized sites, the global non-vacuity check still passes. This contradicts the stated `with any flag order` behavior and leaves the skew guard bypassable by an ordinary command reordering. The self-test has no case for this valid spelling.
issues.fix_hint: Parse each live command sufficiently to identify `cargo install` invocations whose crate argument is `wasm-pack` regardless of option ordering, then validate the associated `--version` value. Add self-tests for at least `cargo install --locked wasm-pack` (must fail as unpinned), `cargo install --version 0.15.0 --locked wasm-pack` (must pass), and a wrong pre-crate version (must fail).
issues.title: Scanner misses cargo options placed before the crate name

verdict.summary: The central pin and current workflow edits are consistent, and both the self-test and repository scan pass. However, the new gate does not recognize a valid cargo-install spelling that its own comments claim to support, so future workflow edits can introduce an unpinned wasm-pack install without failing the gate.
